scope_note: Hand-authored gloss seed for the Apannaka-jataka (ch. 1), Task 21. Layer-5 editorial voice; linguistic register per the Commentary Mockup's Jetavana specimen. The Jetavana / sophists / Anathapindika glosses carry the design-approved specimen copy. Terms are verbatim strings from Chalmers 1895; pid anchors the first occurrence. Authored by the terminal side as the task-directed seed — steward review pending; no AI generation.

glosses.etym: “Jeta's grove” — jeta (the prince who owned it) + vana, grove
glosses.body: The monastery park outside Sāvatthi, bought for the Order by Anāthapiṇḍika — by tradition at the price of covering the ground in gold. Most Jātaka frame-stories open here.

glosses.etym: Pāli form of Sanskrit Śrāvastī, capital of the Kosala kingdom
glosses.body: The city where the Buddha spent most of his teaching years; Jetavana lies just outside it. Chalmers prints the Pāli name without diacritics, as his 1895 edition did.

glosses.etym: Chalmers' rendering of titthiyā, followers of rival teachers
glosses.body: A Victorian translator's choice: the Pāli names adherents of the six non-Buddhist schools, and Chalmers reaches for the Greek word his readers knew for professional rival teachers.

glosses.etym: Chalmers' rendering of seṭṭhi — guild-master, banker, man of means
glosses.body: Not a court official but a great merchant-banker. “The Treasurer” throughout the frame stories is Anāthapiṇḍika; the past-life narratives have their own seṭṭhis of Benares.

glosses.etym: “feeder of the destitute” — an epithet of Sudatta, banker of Sāvatthi
glosses.body: The Buddha's great lay patron, donor of Jetavana. “The Treasurer” throughout the Jātaka's frame stories is this man.

glosses.etym: Chalmers' rendering of bhikkhu — mendicant monk of the Order
glosses.body: The ordained monks of the Buddha's Order (saṅgha). The capitalised “Brethren” is the translation's period convention for the community as an institution.

glosses.etym: Chalmers' rendering of yakkha (Skt. yakṣa), a class of non-human beings
glosses.body: In this tale the yakkhas conjure a false oasis to lure the foolish caravan to its destruction. Rendered variously as goblins, ogres, or demons across the archive's translations; the archive preserves each translator's choice.

glosses.etym: Pāli — “a being (satta) bound for awakening (bodhi)”; Skt. bodhisattva
glosses.body: The Buddha in his former births. Every Jātaka identifies the Bodhisatta among its past-life characters — here, the prudent merchant whose discernment saves his caravan.

glosses.etym: the English name of Vārāṇasī, on the Ganges
glosses.body: The stock opening of the Jātaka's past-life narratives — “when Brahmadatta was reigning in Benares” — places the story in a legendary India before the Buddha's own age.

glosses.etym: Pāli sattha, a trading caravan; satthavāha, its leader
glosses.body: The five-hundred-cart trading caravan is the tale's stage. The caravan-leader (satthavāha) is a recurring Bodhisatta role across the Jātaka — the figure whose judgment carries many lives.
